L12: ## Transfer Credit Policies at the University of Maine at Presque Isle
L13: 
L14: Board of Trustees transfer policies provide the maximum opportunity for transfer both into and within the University of Maine System (UMS).  The following transfer practices are endorsed and followed by the UMS.
L15: ### Transfer Credit within the UMS
L16:   1. All undergraduate courses successfully completed with a grade of C- or higher, including P grades, will transfer from one UMS institution to another. Grades will be recorded on the student’s transcript but not computed into the Grade Point Average (GPA). Semester and cumulative grade point averages reflect only those courses taken at UMPI. Students who are enrolled in multi-university degree programs should inquire about any exceptions that may apply.
L17:   2.
L18: Students who have completed the UMS General Education Transfer Block at one UMS institution will be regarded as having completed their general education requirements at every other UMS institution, with the exception of up to 11 credits of general education coursework specified by the receiving institution. Students who are interested should contact the Office of Student Records/Registrar’s Office at the institution where the general education requirements were completed in order to have the block certification verified and added to their academic record.
L19:   3. Additional grade or credit requirements may exist at the institution or program level at UMPI.
L20: ### Transfer Credit from External Institutions
L21:   1. Transfer students must request that official transcripts be sent directly from all previous institutions to the UMS Shared Processing Center.  Electronic transcripts may be sent to edocs@maine.edu or paper copies may be sent to Application Processing, University of Maine System, P.O. Box 412, Bangor, ME 04402-0412.
L22:   2. To qualify for transfer credit within the UMS, courses must be successfully completed with a grade of C- or higher at an accredited institution of higher learning that is recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or the United States Department of Education (USDE), or the American Council on Education (ACE).  The student’s transfer credits will not be computed into the Grade Point Average (GPA).
L23:   3. Courses taken under a P, S, or CR grade at an institution external to the UMS must have the “Passing” grade defined as being equal to a grade of C- or higher to qualify for transfer within the UMS.
L24:   4. Course credit originating from international institutions may qualify for transfer consistent with established institutional policies.
L25:   5. Transfer students are required to satisfy residency requirements at UMPI.
L26:   6. Students transferring from the Maine Community College System (MCCS) into the UMS, who have completed the General Education Transfer Block (as noted on their MCCS institution’s official transcript), will be regarded as having completed the UMS general education requirements, with the exception of up to 11 credits of general education coursework to be specified by the receiving institution.
L27: ### Transfer Evaluations
L28:   1. Transfer credit evaluations will be completed for admitted students and will be available to view within the Student Center in MaineStreet.  Transfer students should meet with either their Professional Academic Advisor/New Student Enrollment Specialist/YourPace Academic Success Coach to review how the awarded credits may be applied toward their degree plan.
L29:   2. Students with coursework from schools which are not recognized by the Council for Higher Education Accreditation (CHEA) or the United States Department of Education (USDE) as being accredited institutions of higher learning may inquire into the possibility of validating some or all of their learning through testing and/or approved institutional Credit for Prior Learning (CPL) processes.
L30:   3. Coursework defined as developmental or remedial by UMPI is considered preparatory to college-level work and will not be awarded transfer credit.
L31:   4. Transfer students will be expected to meet the established requirements of the academic program, college and/or degree plan into which they are transferring.  Students should consult UMPI’s catalog and/or meet with an appropriate advisor to determine requirements regarding the number and distribution of credits that must be completed to earn the desired degree. Students should meet with their assigned advisor to review their Degree Progress Report (DPR) generated in MaineStreet.
L32:   5. Students may confer with their assigned advisor about the transfer credit evaluation process. This process may entail a request for a re-evaluation through the appropriate channels. The appropriate application of transfer credit is the responsibility of the relevant academic unit (college or department). If a student disagrees with the transfer credit re-evaluation after completing this process, the student then goes to the Academic Appeals Board.
L33:   6. Current UMS semester-based students who plan to take courses at another institution, inside or outside of the UMS, are strongly encouraged to seek prior approval of their plans by completing a Domestic or International Study Away Form at the institution where they are matriculated.
L34:   7. Repeat to replace regarding transfer credit. Students may elect to repeat a previously taken course. Upon review of the student’s Degree Progress Report (DPR), their Professional Academic Advisor/New Student Enrollment Specialist/YourPace Academic Success Coach will either register the student for the repeated UMPI course or approve the outside transfer credit.
L35: Coursework completed at another institution may be used to replace a UMPI course grade, provided that the transfer course is deemed equivalent in content to the UMPI course. In such cases, the original UMPI grade will be excluded from GPA calculations, and no new grade will be factored in. Neither grade will be counted in the term or cumulative GPA.
L36:   8. Once a student has satisfied all degree requirements, no additional transfer credits will be accepted or applied toward the completed program of study.

L29: # FAQs
L30: 
L31: The YourPace program at the University of Maine at Presque Isle represents competency-based learning at its best, allowing you to progress through earning your undergraduate or graduate degree more efficiently, while focusing on the learning you need. Since not everybody is familiar with this approach, here are answers to frequently asked questions about YourPace at UMPI.
L32: ### What is YourPace?
L33: The UMPI YourPace program is an innovative, competency-based way for you to earn your degree on your terms. The programs are delivered in online, eight-week sessions, using a digital platform. Each course you take is built around learning modules with embedded competencies. You progress as you demonstrate mastery of each competency. Once you demonstrate mastery of all competencies and successfully complete your final assessment, you have completed the course.
L34: Since you determine how many courses to complete during each eight-week session, you have more control over your schedule and how quickly you progress toward completing your degree.
L35: ### Are YourPace programs accredited?
L36: 
L37: Yes, the YourPace program is accredited by 【22†The New England Commission of Higher Education (NECHE).†www.neche.org】
L38: ### What are the admissions requirements?
L39: Applicants must be at least 20 years of age at the time of application, unless they have previously earned a bachelor’s or an associate’s degree from an accredited institution. Applicants must submit a clear copy of a valid, government-issued photo identification. Applicants must have a high school diploma or equivalent. Applicants must submit all official transcripts. They must have a minimum cumulative college GPA of 1.75 from the most recently attended institution.
L40: Visit the 【11†YourPace Admissions Requirements page】 for more information about admissions requirements.
L41: ### What are the technology requirements?
L42: 
L43: To successfully participate in UMPI’s online programs, students must have access to appropriate technology and possess basic technical skills.
L44: #### Required Device
L45: 
L46:   * A reliable desktop or laptop computer (Windows or Mac) capable of running standard productivity software and accessing online learning platforms
L47:   * Chromebooks may allow for basic access, but they are not recommended as they may not support all required coursework activities
L48:   * Smartphones and tablets are not sufficient as a primary device for coursework
L49: #### Software & Course Tools
L50: 
L51:   * Microsoft Office 365 is provided at no cost to UMPI students and is commonly used for coursework
L52: 
L53: #### Internet Access
L54: 
L55:   * Reliable, high-speed internet access is required to participate in online courses, access learning materials, and submit assignments
L56: 
L57: #### Audio & Video Capabilities
L58: 
L59:   * A webcam and microphone are required for activities such as recorded presentations, voiceovers, and video-based assignments
L60: #### Basic Technology Skills
L61: 
L62: Students should be able to:
L63: 
L64:   * Power on their device and connect to the internet
L65:   * Navigate a web browser and access online platforms
L66:   * Save files to their computer
L67:   * Download and upload files such as PDFs, Word documents, and spreadsheets
L68: ### How can I earn credit for my prior work experience?
L69: 
L70: Credit for Prior Learning Assessment (CPL) represents a process designed to give students course credit based on prior knowledge they have gained through experience outside of the classroom. We have a variety of different options that are available to you as a YourPace student and these include testing, certifications, and portfolio creation. You can get much more information on this process by talking to a member of our YourPace team.
L71: ### How long will it take me to complete my program?
L72: 
L73: That depends entirely on you! The amount of time it takes is dependent on the number of credits transferred in and the time you have to study and complete your competency work. Proving your knowledge by satisfying competencies through assessments means that you may significantly shorten the length of time it takes to complete your degree, as well as decreasing the total cost of the program.
L74: ### How many credit hours can I transfer?
L75: 
L76: There is no set limit to the number of credits you can transfer into UMPI. Transfer credits are evaluated to determine how they apply toward your chosen program and degree requirements.
L77: 
L78: However, students must still meet UMPI residency requirements in order to earn a degree:
L79:   * Four-year degree programs (baccalaureate): Students must complete at least 30 credit hours through UMPI. At least 12 of these credits must be in the major, and at least 9 of those 12 credits must be at the upper level (300-level or above).
L80:   * Two-year degree programs: Students must complete at least 15 credit hours through UMPI.
L81: Transfer credit evaluations are generally applied to your academic record regardless of major; however, how those credits apply toward degree requirements may change if you change your major.
L82: ### Are international students eligible?
L83: 
L84: Yes, international students are eligible to apply and enroll; however, an I-20 will NOT be provided as this is a fully online degree program.  In addition to the standard admissions requirements, international students must also meet the additional requirements specific to international applicants. International student questions can be directed to umpi-yourpace@maine.edu or (207) 768-9433.
L85: ### Are international students required to submit English language proficiency exam scores?
L86: 
L87: All international student applicants must request that an official English language proficiency exam score is submitted to the Application Processing Center (edocs@maine.edu) directly by the testing agency.
L88:   * Only tests from the following will be accepted:
L89:   * TOEFL/TOEFL iBT minimum required score of 4 (as of January 21, 2026. Prior to that, a score of 79 was the minimum required). A score of 550 is required for paper-based tests.
L90:   * TOEFL Essentials score of 8.5
L91:   * IELTS score of 6.5
L92:   * Pearson Test of English score of 53
L93:   * Duolingo English Test score of 105
L94:   * Cambridge C1 Advanced
L95: 
L96: Please use 3008 as the institutional code for the official scores.
L97: ### Can the requirement for international students to submit English language proficiency exam scores be waived?
L98: 
L99: Please note: All courses in the YourPace Program are delivered in English, and students are required to submit all coursework, both written and oral assignments, in English.
L100: If you are an international student or a student living in the United States whose first language is not English, you are required to provide proof of English language proficiency. Please review the information below for details on approved exams and potential waiver options.
L101: The University of Maine at Presque Isle Admissions Office considers all applicants under a holistic review process based on the documents required for the application process. English proficiency is required as part of the application process.
L102: 
L103: Potential English proficiency test waivers within the application process:
L104: 
L105: The only guaranteed method of meeting the English proficiency requirement is by passing an English proficiency test.
L106: An English proficiency test waiver may be considered for the application process if one of the following options is met:
L107:   * Your high school transcript clearly states that English is the language of instruction for all subjects.
L108:   * Must have earned one of the following from an institution located within the U.S., Canada, England, Australia, or New Zealand, where English is the primary language of instruction and assessment:
L109:     * Associate’s, Bachelor’s, or Graduate degree from an accredited institution.
L110:     * 60 undergraduate or 12 graduate semester credits from an accredited institution.
L111:   * English is your first or primary language, and you reside in one of the following countries. Verification in the form of a government-issued identification card will be required.

L151: ### How is a competency-based education course designed?
L152: 
L153: In competency-based education, courses are designed to help you build and demonstrate mastery of clearly defined skills and knowledge areas. Instead of focusing on seat time or lectures, you progress by showing what you know and can do.
L154: Each course is structured around competencies, and learning is supported through curated course materials, activities, and practice opportunities that help you build understanding at your own pace. Courses include milestones, which are assignments such as discussions, quizzes, case studies, projects, or written work. These milestones help you apply what you are learning and prepare you for the final assessment.
L155: At the end of the course, you complete a final assessment, which is the opportunity to demonstrate full mastery of the course competencies. This format is designed to support independent learning while still providing structure, feedback, and clear checkpoints throughout the course.

L100: ## 【29†Admissions】
L101: 
L102: Review the categories listed below to learn details about admission at University of Massachusetts Global. If you still have questions and concerns, contact an enrollment coach. For other resources pertaining to admission see 【36†Admission Resources】.
L103: 
L104: ## Admissions FAQs
L105: 
L106: ### Apply
L107: #### [Button: Can I make changes to the information on my application? ]
L108: 
L109: Yes, but the process differs depending on the requested change.
L110: 
L111:   * Change Contact Information: If you need to update your contact information, fill out and submit the 【51†update contact information】 form. You can also email the changes you are requesting to apply@umassglobal.edu.
L112:   * Change Start Term / Program of Choice: Email your request to enroll@umassglobal.edu, and an enrollment coach will assist you.
L113: #### [Button: How do I apply to University of Massachusetts Global? ]
L114: 
L115: UMass Global has a fully online application at 【52†www.umassglobal.edu/apply】.
L116: #### [Button: Is there an application fee? ]
L117: 
L118: No, there is no application fee to apply to UMass Global. This aligns with our commitment to affordability and to serving busy working adults, many of whom are balancing jobs, parenting, and other responsibilities while they finish their degree. By removing the fee and keeping the process easy to apply, students can take the first step toward their goals without an upfront cost or added barrier.
L119: #### [Button: Who can assist me with the application process? ]
L120: 
L121: Your enrollment coach is your main point of contact for your application status, requirements, and next steps. They can answer most general questions about programs, deadlines, and what to submit, and will help you stay on track as you move toward enrollment.​
L122: 
L123: If you have not yet been contacted by an enrollment coach, you can call (800) 746-0082 or email enroll@umassglobal.edu to be connected with someone who can support you.

L133: #### [Button: When will I find out if I’m admitted, and how will I be notified? ]
L134:

L136: 
L137: You’ll receive your official admission decision by email from the Office of Admission, and then your enrollment coach will reach out to walk you through your next steps and answer any questions.
L138: #### [Button: What if I need to start in a later term? ]

L156: ### Credit for Prior Learning
L157: #### [Button: What is Credit for Prior Learning? ]
L158: 
L159: Credit for Prior Learning may help you earn credit for learning completed outside a traditional college course. Depending on your program and the learning you can document, this may include military training, professional certifications, workforce training, qualifying exams, ACE-recommended learning, or portfolio assessment.
L160: 
L161: UMass Global reviews your documentation and determines whether credit may apply to your degree.
L162: #### [Button: Does an ACE recommendation mean I will receive credit? ]
L163: 
L164: Not always. An ACE recommendation can show that your learning may be eligible for review. UMass Global decides whether credit applies to your degree based on your documentation, program requirements, and current academic policies.
L165: #### [Button: How much Credit for Prior Learning can I apply to my undergraduate degree? ]
L166: 
L167: Credit from other credit opportunities is generally limited to 25% of the credits required for an undergraduate degree. That is up to 15 credits in a 60-credit associate degree or up to 30 credits in a 120-credit bachelor’s degree.
L168: Some types of credit are not included in this limit, including ACE-evaluated credit and eligible AP, CLEP, DSST, IB, DLAT, and DLPT exams. Program requirements and residency requirements may still apply.
L169: ### Transcripts
L170: 
L171: #### [Button: Can I use my unofficial transcripts to be admitted? ]
L172: 
L173: Yes, we can start processing your application with your unofficial transcripts. You may upload them to the Education History section of the online application for admission or email them to admtranscripts@umassglobal.edu to expedite your admission.
L174: 
L175: Official transcripts are still required and must be submitted by the end of your first session.
L176: #### [Button: What is an "official" transcript? ]
L177: 
L178: An official transcript is one sent directly from the institution of record to University of Massachusetts Global.
L179: 
L180: #### Electronic Transcripts
L181: 
L182: Electronic transcripts must be sent from your previous institution directly to us - University of Massachusetts Global Admissions Office at admtranscripts@umassglobal.edu. Electronic transcripts that have been emailed to the applicant and then forwarded to the Admissions Office are not considered official.
L183: #### Paper Transcripts
L184: 
L185: Paper transcripts sent via mail must arrive at UMass Global's Admissions Office in a sealed envelope from the institution of record. A transcript issued to the applicant may be accepted if it is delivered in the official unopened and sealed envelope from the institution of record.
L186: 
L187: #### [Button: Do all programs require transcripts? ]
L188: 
L189: No. Transcripts are not required for the added authorization credential programs, or the California Teacher of English Learners (CTEL) authorization.
L190: #### [Button: What transcripts are required to be submitted for admission? ]
L191: 
L192: Admission requirements vary by program. Check the 【15†current catalog†catalog.umassglobal.edu】 for specific requirements related to your program of interest. When filling out the online application, you must list your complete academic history regardless of the transcript requirements. This includes all colleges, universities, career institutions, military institutions, etc., where you earned academic credit.
L193:   * Undergraduate: If you are applying to any of our undergraduate programs, transcripts are required from all institutions previously attended.
L194:   * Graduate: If you are applying to one of our graduate programs, we require you to submit transcripts from the highest level, most recently earned degree from an institutionally accredited institution (bachelor's, master's, or doctoral). If graduate-level or credential coursework was taken after the bachelor’s degree, regardless of whether a master’s or other graduate-level degree or credential was completed, those transcripts are required in addition to the bachelor’s degree transcripts.
